scenes.text: November 2004: four releases that changed gaming, in one month.
On November ninth, Halo 2 arrived on Xbox and took in one hundred twenty-five million dollars on day one.
A week later, Half-Life 2 hit PC with physics puzzles, and it needed Steam to play.
On November twenty-first, the Nintendo DS launched in North America with two screens, for one forty-nine ninety-nine.
Two days later came World of Warcraft, which would peak at twelve million subscribers.

stories.headline: Halo 2 launches on Xbox
stories.takeaway: Matchmaking and parties made online play easy on Xbox Live.
points: Developed by Bungie, published by Microsoft
Campaign adds the Arbiter as a playable lead

stories.headline: Half-Life 2 arrives on PC
stories.takeaway: Physics became gameplay, and Steam became a requirement.
points: Gravity Gun turns objects into tools

stories.headline: Nintendo DS launches
stories.takeaway: A handheld with two screens, one of them a touchscreen.

stories.headline: World of Warcraft goes live
stories.takeaway: It went on to become the most-subscribed MMORPG ever.
points: Launched in North America, Australia and NZ
